---
title: "*Iliad* + *scholia* reader"
---

## Overview

[`iliad-scholia`](https://neelsmith.github.io/hmt-apps/iliad-scholia.html):  Read a passage of the *Iliad* in a Homer Multitext edition together with *scholia* on the passage, in the context of the manuscript page it is on.

## User options and display

- Choose the **Version of the *Iliad*** (versions with no online text are listed but disabled) and, when it has both, the **Text**: diplomatic or normalized.
- The count for a line is the number of scholia indexed to it in the version being read.
- Enter a **Passage**: a line (`1.5`), a range (`1.1-1.10`) or a whole book (`1`); the example buttons fill the field, and a note shows which books the text has. Press **Show**.
- The display lists the lines grouped by manuscript page (at most 2,000 lines and 40 pages), each line with a badge counting its scholia; clicking the badge unfolds them. Requested lines are marked. A note lists passages the DSE does not place on a page.
- **Unfold all scholia** opens or folds every scholion on a page.
- Every manuscript page in the page view has **‹ Previous page** and **Next page ›** buttons (the page before or after in the codex; the first and last page of a codex have one button disabled). These reopen the app at the *Iliad* lines on the neighbouring page (skipping pages with no indexed text); the address becomes the `?text=…` range of that page, in the version of the page, so the version menu may change.
- Changing the version or text re-runs the display.


## Optional parameters


- `text` — a CTS URN, shows all text indexed to that page, highlighting the requested passage. Example: `?text=urn:cts:greekLit:tlg0012.tlg001.msA:1.1-1.10`. 
- `page`  — a page URN. Shows text indexed to that page.
- `image` —  an image URN. Shows the text indexed to that image.


If multiple parameters are given, `text` takes priority, then `page`, then `image`.


## Data sources

From the HMT release

- `#!ctscatalog` and `#!ctsdata`: the texts.
- `#!citerelationset`: DSE records
- `#!datamodels`, `#!citecollections` and `#!citedata`: the codices and their pages

A saved copy of a release can be dropped on the page or chosen with the file picker.

## Output options

None.
